hook.situation: You're telling a Korean friend why you missed a meeting. You say '비가 와서 못 왔어요' — fine, but flat. A natural Korean speaker would say '비가 오는 바람에 못 왔어요' (the rain swept in and derailed my plans) or '비가 오길래 그냥 집에 있었어요' (I noticed the rain coming, so I just stayed home). Same fact. Completely different nuance. After this chapter you'll choose the RIGHT connector, not just any connector.
objectives: Use -더니 to narrate observed patterns that led to a result
Use -길래 to explain a spontaneous reaction to something you personally noticed
Use -는 바람에 for an unexpected cause that disrupted the plan
Use -(으)ㄹ수록 for 'the more X, the more Y' proportional relationships
Use -기 위해서 to state a clear purpose
hook.whyItMatters: Beginners connect ideas with 그래서 and -아서/어서 for everything. Intermediate speakers choose from a richer toolkit: -더니 signals you WITNESSED something over time, -길래 signals you REACTED on the spot, -는 바람에 signals an unexpected disruption, -(으)ㄹ수록 signals a proportional relationship, and -기 위해서 gives a clear purpose. Using the right connector is what makes your Korean sound like a real person talking, not a grammar textbook.

grammarNotes.title: -더니 — "and then (I noticed)…"
grammarNotes.func: Links two clauses where you personally saw or noticed situation X, and then Y followed — as a result or as a contrast. The first clause is something you observed (usually about someone or something else), not a plan of your own.

formTable.when: After a verb or adjective stem
Your own past action → present result

examples.ko: 동생이 아까 울더니 지금은 자고 있어요.
examples.romanization: dongsaeng-i akka uldeoni jigeum-eun jago isseoyo.
examples.en: My little brother was crying a moment ago, and now he's sleeping.
examples.note: Plain -더니: I watched him cry, then a new state followed (contrast).

examples.ko: 친구가 열심히 공부하더니 시험을 잘 봤어요.
examples.romanization: chingu-ga yeolsimhi gongbuhadeoni siheom-eul jal bwasseoyo.
examples.en: My friend studied hard, and (sure enough) did well on the test.
examples.note: X (effort I saw) leads to Y (result); the subject is someone else.

examples.ko: 아침에는 날씨가 좋더니 오후에 비가 왔어요.
examples.romanization: achim-eneun nalssi-ga jotdeoni ohu-e bi-ga wasseoyo.
examples.en: The weather was nice in the morning, and then it rained in the afternoon.
examples.note: -더니 with an adjective (좋다), showing a contrast between two times.

examples.ko: 밥을 많이 먹었더니 배가 너무 불러요.
examples.romanization: bap-eul mani meogeotdeoni bae-ga neomu bulleoyo.
examples.en: I ate a lot, so now I'm really full.
examples.note: -았/었더니 with a first-person subject: my own past action causing a present result.

keyPoint.label: -더니 vs. -았/었더니
keyPoint.body: Use plain -더니 when you noticed someone else's situation (친구가 공부하더니… = my friend studied, and then…). Use -았/었더니 when YOU did the action and report the result now (제가 먹었더니… = I ate, so now…). Why the past form attaches the way it does is a later topic — for now, just pair plain -더니 with 'someone else' and -았/었더니 with 'I'.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 좋더니 sounds like [조터니] — the ㅎ blends with the following ㄷ into an aspirated [ㅌ].

drill.instruction: Join the two facts into one sentence with -더니 (use -았/었더니 if the subject is 저/나).
drill.model: 동생이 울다 / 지금 자다 → 동생이 울더니 지금 자요.
items: 아침에 머리가 아프다 / 약을 먹고 괜찮아지다 → ____
제가 커피를 많이 마시다 / 잠이 안 오다 → ____ (use -았/었더니)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers stick plain -더니 onto their own actions like a simple 'and then.' But plain -더니 reports something you noticed about others; for your own finished action that leads to a result, you need the past form -았/었더니.

grammarNotes.title: -길래 — "since I saw…, I…"
grammarNotes.func: Gives the reason behind your own reaction or decision: because you noticed situation X, you did Y. The first clause is an outside trigger you observed; the second is your own spontaneous response.

examples.ko: 가게에서 과일이 싸길래 좀 많이 샀어요.
examples.romanization: gage-eseo gwail-i ssagillae jom mani sasseoyo.
examples.en: The fruit was cheap at the store, so I bought quite a lot.
examples.note: X (I noticed it was cheap) triggers my reaction Y (bought a lot).

examples.en: My friend looked hungry, so I bought them a meal.
examples.note: The trigger is someone else's state; my reaction is the kind gesture.

examples.en: The weather was nice, so I went for a walk with a friend.
examples.note: -길래 with an adjective; the second clause must be the speaker's own action.

examples.en: The book was fun, so I read it all the way to the end.
examples.note: Reason (the book was fun) → my resulting action (finished reading).

keyPoint.label: -길래 vs. -아서/-니까
keyPoint.body: -아서 and -니까 give a plain reason for almost any clause, including requests and suggestions. -길래 is narrower: the reason is something you yourself noticed, and the result is your own (usually past) action — you can't say 비싸길래 사지 마세요. When telling someone else to do something, use -니까.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 맛있길래 sounds like [마싣낄래] — the ㄱ of 길 tenses to [ㄲ] after the preceding consonant.

drill.instruction: Make one sentence with -길래 (a reason you noticed + your own past reaction).
drill.model: 과일이 싸다 / 많이 사다 → 과일이 싸길래 많이 샀어요.
items: 친구가 영화를 보고 싶어 하다 / 같이 가다 → ____

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'since/because' works fine before a command, so learners attach -길래 to requests. But -길래 only leads into your own past action, never a command or suggestion. Switch to -니까 when you're telling someone else to do something.

grammarNotes.title: -는 바람에 — "because of (something unexpected)…"
grammarNotes.func: Gives a sudden, usually unwanted cause for a bad or unintended result. It signals that X threw things off and Y happened against your plans.

formTable.ex: 놓치다 → 놓치는 바람에 / 자다 → 자는 바람에

formTable.when: Verb stem ending in ㄹ (ㄹ drops)
formTable.ex: 울다 → 우는 바람에 / 놀다 → 노는 바람에

examples.en: I overslept, so (unfortunately) I was late to school.
examples.note: Unexpected cause (oversleeping) → unwanted result (being late).

examples.en: I missed the bus, so I was late to meet up.
examples.note: Classic disruption pattern; the result is a setback.

examples.ko: 동생이 우는 바람에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.romanization: dongsaeng-i uneun barame jam-eul mot jasseoyo.
examples.en: My little brother kept crying, so I couldn't sleep.
examples.note: 울다 → 우는: ㄹ drops before -는. The cause is someone else's action.

examples.ko: 비가 갑자기 오는 바람에 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.romanization: bi-ga gapjagi oneun barame os-i da jeojeosseoyo.
examples.en: It suddenly rained, so my clothes got all wet.
examples.note: 갑자기 (suddenly) fits the 'unexpected disruption' feel of this form.

keyPoint.label: -는 바람에 vs. -아서/-어서
keyPoint.body: -아서/-어서 states a plain cause for any kind of result, good or bad. -는 바람에 is saved for an unexpected cause that leads to a bad or unplanned result, and the second clause is normally in the past tense. You wouldn't say 열심히 공부하는 바람에 시험을 잘 봤어요 — for a good result, use -아서/-어서.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 늦는 sounds like [는는] in fast speech — the ㅈ of 늦 becomes [ㄴ] before the ㄴ of 는.

drill.instruction: Join the two facts with -는 바람에 (unexpected cause → bad result, second clause in past tense).
drill.model: 늦잠을 자다 / 학교에 늦다 → 늦잠을 자는 바람에 학교에 늦었어요.
items: 휴대폰을 잃어버리다 / 친구한테 연락 못 하다 → ____

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners use -는 바람에 for any cause, like a neutral 'because.' But -는 바람에 only fits an unexpected cause with a bad result. For a good result you brought about, use -아서/-어서 or -(은)ㄴ 덕분에 ('thanks to').

grammarNotes.title: -(으)ㄹ수록 — the more …, the more …
grammarNotes.func: -(으)ㄹ수록 attaches to a verb or adjective stem to mean "the more X happens, the more Y." It links a rising cause to a rising result, and is often paired with 점점 ("more and more").

formTable.add: + 수록 (do not add 을 or another ㄹ)
formTable.ex: 살다 → 살수록 · 알다 → 알수록 · 길다 → 길수록

formTable.when: Often doubled with the same verb + -(으)면

examples.en: The more I study Korean, the more fun it is.
examples.note: 공부하다 → 공부할수록 (vowel stem → ㄹ수록).

examples.en: The more I see my friend, the more I like them.
examples.note: 만나다 → 만날수록.

examples.en: The more I read this book, the harder it gets.
examples.note: 읽다 → 읽을수록 (consonant stem → 을수록).

examples.en: The more I look, the prettier it is.
examples.note: The doubled 보면 볼수록 frame is very common in speech.

keyPoint.label: Pair it with 점점
keyPoint.body: -(으)ㄹ수록 often comes with 점점 ("gradually, more and more") to stress the rising effect: 시간이 갈수록 점점 추워져요 ("as time goes on, it gets colder and colder"). The doubled V-(으)면 V-(으)ㄹ수록 form (알면 알수록) is a fixed, natural way to say "the more … the more."

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 읽을수록 is pronounced [일글쑤록]: the ㄱ links onto the following vowel and 수 tenses to [쑤].

drill.instruction: Make "the more …, the more …" sentences — follow the model.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Don't drop the (으)ㄹ. A vowel stem still needs the ㄹ (공부할수록), and a consonant stem needs 을 (먹을수록). It is never just stem + 수록.

grammarNotes.title: -기 위해서 — in order to / for the sake of
grammarNotes.func: -기 위해서 marks a purpose — the goal you do something for. Attach -기 위해서 to a verb stem ("in order to V"), or N을/를 위해서 to a noun ("for the sake of N"). The 서 is optional: 위해 = 위해서.

formTable.when: Verb stem + 기 위해서 ("in order to V")
formTable.ex: 배우다 → 배우기 위해서 · 사다 → 사기 위해서
건강 → 건강을 위해서 · 친구 → 친구를 위해서

examples.en: I came to Korea (in order) to learn Korean.
examples.note: 배우다 → 배우기 위해서. The goal comes first, the action second.

examples.en: I exercise every day for my health.
examples.note: Noun goal → 건강을 위해서.

examples.ko: 시험을 잘 보기 위해서 열심히 공부해요.
examples.romanization: si-heo-meul jal bo-gi wi-hae-seo yeol-sim-hi gong-bu-hae-yo.
examples.en: I study hard (in order) to do well on the exam.
examples.note: 보다 → 보기 위해서.

examples.en: I bought a gift for my friend.
examples.note: Noun + 를 위해서 = "for (the sake of)."

keyPoint.label: -기 위해서 vs -(으)러
keyPoint.body: Both express purpose, but -(으)러 attaches only to a verb and only pairs with going/coming verbs (가다/오다): 밥 먹으러 가요 (I go to eat). -기 위해서 is broader — any verb, any main clause, and it can also take a noun goal (건강을 위해서). Use -(으)러 for "go/come to do," and -기 위해서 for any purpose.

drill.instruction: State a purpose — follow the model.
drill.model: (한국어를 배우다 / 한국에 오다) → 한국어를 배우기 위해서 한국에 왔어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Don't forget the -기 that turns the verb into a noun-like form. It is verb-stem + 기 + 위해서 (배우기 위해서), never just verb + 위해서.

exampleSentence.en: The event got cancelled because of the rain.
exampleSentence.note: 취소되다 is passive — the subject is what was cancelled, not who cancelled it

exampleSentence.ko: 갑자기 비가 오는 바람에 옷이 다 젖었어요.
exampleSentence.en: My clothes got completely soaked because it suddenly started raining.
exampleSentence.note: 바람에 carries the nuance that the cause was unexpected or unwelcome, stronger than 때문에

exampleSentence.en: The more you practice, the fewer mistakes you make.
exampleSentence.note: Perfect partner for -(으)ㄹ수록: proportional improvement through practice

exampleSentence.en: The more you practice, the more your skills improve.
exampleSentence.note: 늘다 (to grow/increase) pairs naturally with 실력

exampleSentence.en: The more you use Korean, the more your skills grow.
exampleSentence.note: 늘다 is intransitive — the subject improves on its own; contrast with 늘리다 (to increase something intentionally)

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 매일 야식을 먹더니 살이 찐 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: My friend kept eating late-night snacks, and it seems they gained weight.
exampleSentence.note: Classic -더니 scenario: you observed the habit over time → you're now noting the result

exampleSentence.en: They've been stressed lately, and they've gained weight.
exampleSentence.note: 살이 찌다 is an expression — 살 (flesh/fat) + 이 (subject marker) + 찌다 (to fatten/swell)

exampleSentence.en: It was clear, and then suddenly there was thunder.
exampleSentence.note: 갑자기 intensifies the contrast in -더니 sentences — the unexpected shift

exampleSentence.en: They kept working hard, and in the end they passed.
exampleSentence.note: 결국 often appears in the result clause of -더니 sentences, marking the endpoint of the observed sequence

exampleSentence.en: The more experience accumulates, the more confidence you gain.
exampleSentence.note: 쌓이다 is the passive of 쌓다 (to stack/pile); -ㄹ수록 pairs perfectly with gradual accumulation

exampleSentence.en: Korean food has more charm the more you know about it.
exampleSentence.note: 알다 (ㄹ-stem) drops ㄹ → 알수록. 매력이 있다 = to have charm/appeal

exampleSentence.en: The ratings were low, and in the end the drama was cancelled.
exampleSentence.note: 폐지되다 is the passive of 폐지하다 (to abolish/cancel); -더니 here: you observed the low ratings → you're reporting the outcome

exampleSentence.en: The more success experiences accumulate, the higher your self-confidence rises.
exampleSentence.note: 자신 (self/oneself) + 감 (feeling/sense) — a great -(으)ㄹ수록 vocabulary word

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 요즘 너무 피곤하더니 결국 쓰러졌어요.
exampleSentence.en: My friend seemed so exhausted lately, and they finally collapsed.
exampleSentence.note: -더니 with an adjective: the speaker observed the state of exhaustion over time → reports the result

exampleSentence.en: The more effort you put in, the greater the sense of fulfillment you feel.
exampleSentence.note: 보람 is a uniquely Korean concept for the rewarding feeling that comes from effort well spent

exampleSentence.en: Korean seemed hard at first, and now it's gotten easier.
exampleSentence.note: -더니 with an adjective: earlier observation (it WAS hard) contrasted with a current changed state (now it's easy)

extendedVocabulary.english: to get used to / become accustomed

exampleSentence.en: The more you use it, the more accustomed you become.
exampleSentence.note: 익숙하다 (familiar/accustomed) + -아/어지다 (become) = getting used to. Perfect -(으)ㄹ수록 partner

extendedDialogue.setting: Jiyeon and her coworker Hyunwoo chat over coffee after a colleague's promotion

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 민준 씨가 몇 달 동안 매일 야근하더니 결국 팀장이 됐어요.
lines.romanization: Minjun ssiga myeot dal dongan maeil yageunhadeoni gyeolguk timjangi dwaesseoyo.
lines.en: Minjun worked late every night for months, and in the end he became team leader.
lines.grammarNote: -더니: Jiyeon personally watched the pattern of Minjun's overtime work (camera rolling) and now reports the natural outcome — his promotion

lines.speaker: 현우
lines.ko: 맞아요. 저도 봤어요. 열심히 하더니 잘 됐네요.
lines.romanization: Majayo. Jeodo bwasseoyo. Yeolsimhi hadeoni jal dwaenneyo.
lines.en: That's right. I saw it too. He worked hard and things worked out well.
lines.grammarNote: -더니 again: Hyunwoo confirming he also observed (watched) the same behavior pattern — shared camera footage, so to speak

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 사실 저도 더 노력해야겠다는 생각이 들었어요.
lines.romanization: Sasil jeodo deo noryeokhaeyagettaneun saenggagi deureosseoyo.
lines.en: Honestly, it made me think I should try harder too.
lines.grammarNote: No -더니 here — Jiyeon is talking about her own internal reaction, not an observation about another person

lines.speaker: 현우
lines.ko: 경험이 쌓일수록 기회도 많아지는 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: Gyeongheomi ssahilsurok gihoedo manajineun geot gatayo.
lines.en: It seems like the more experience piles up, the more opportunities come.
lines.grammarNote: 쌓이다 ㄹ-vowel ending → -ㄹ수록. -(으)ㄹ수록 captures the proportional scale: experience ↑ → opportunities ↑

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 맞아요. 일할수록 더 잘 알게 되는 것도 있고요.
lines.romanization: Majayo. Ilhalsurok deo jal alge doeneun geotdo itgoyo.
lines.en: True. And the more you work, the more you come to understand.
lines.grammarNote: 일하다 (consonant-free vowel stem 하) → 할수록 (contracted). Two proportional relationships in one sentence: work ↑ → understanding ↑

lines.speaker: 현우
lines.ko: 그런데 민준 씨가 처음에는 많이 힘들어하더니 이제는 여유가 생겼어요.
lines.romanization: Geureonde Minjun ssiga cheoeumeneun manhi himdeureohadeoni ijeneun yeoyuga saenggyeosseoyo.
lines.en: By the way, Minjun seemed to struggle a lot at first, and now he has breathing room.
lines.grammarNote: -더니 marks the contrast: EARLIER state (observed struggling) vs. CURRENT changed state (now relaxed) — the quintessential use of -더니 for contrast

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 저도 적응할수록 여유가 생길 거라고 믿어요.
lines.romanization: Jeodo jeogeunghalsurok yeoyuga saengil georago mideoyo.
lines.en: I believe the more I adapt, the more breathing room I'll get too.
lines.grammarNote: 적응하다 → 적응할수록. First-person -(으)ㄹ수록 expressing hope/belief about one's own proportional growth

lines.speaker: 현우
lines.ko: 물론이죠. 보면 볼수록 지연 씨도 잘하고 있는 게 보여요.
lines.romanization: Mulronijyo. Bomyeon bolsurok Jiyeon ssido jal hago inneun ge boyeoyo.
lines.en: Of course. The more I watch, the more I can see you're doing well too.
lines.grammarNote: 보면 볼수록: the emphatic -(으)면 V-(으)ㄹ수록 form — the most natural spoken pattern for 'the more X, the more Y'. 보여요 = it becomes visible/apparent

readingText.title: 성장의 기록 (A Record of Growth)
readingText.body: 처음 한국어를 시작했을 때는 발음이 너무 어렵더니 이제는 많이 익숙해졌어요. 그때는 ㄹ과 ㄴ 소리가 비슷하더니 지금은 차이가 잘 들려요. 발음을 고치기 위해서 매일 제 목소리를 녹음했고, 비가 오길래 집에서 혼자 따라 읽은 날도 많았어요. 한 번은 인터넷이 끊기는 바람에 온라인 수업을 못 들었지만, 그날도 포기하지 않고 복습했어요. 공부할수록 더 많은 것이 보이기 시작했어요. 처음에는 드라마 대사가 너무 빠르더니 요즘은 대충 내용을 이해해요. 어휘가 늘수록 한국 문화도 더 깊이 느껴지는 것 같아요. 가끔 힘들 때도 있지만, 노력할수록 보람이 커지는 게 느껴져요. 한국어는 정말 보면 볼수록 매력 있는 언어예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When I first started Korean, the pronunciation was so hard, but now I've gotten very accustomed to it. Back then the ㄹ and ㄴ sounds seemed similar, but now I can hear the difference clearly. To fix my pronunciation, I recorded my voice every day, and on many rainy days I noticed the rain and practiced reading aloud alone at home. Once, because the internet cut out unexpectedly, I missed an online class, but I still reviewed that day without giving up. The more I studied, the more things started to become visible. At first drama dialogue was too fast, but lately I roughly understand the content. The more my vocabulary grows, the more deeply I seem to feel Korean culture too. Sometimes it's difficult, but the more I put in effort, the more I can feel the sense of fulfillment growing. Korean really is a language that gets more charming the more you look at it.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What purpose action did the writer take to improve pronunciation?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 발음을 고치기 위해서 매일 제 목소리를 녹음했어요 — they recorded their voice every day in order to fix pronunciation. This uses -기 위해서 for a planned purpose.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What two cause/reaction connectors appear in the middle of the diary?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 비가 오길래 집에서 혼자 따라 읽은 날도 많았어요 uses -길래: the writer noticed rain and reacted by practicing at home. 인터넷이 끊기는 바람에 온라인 수업을 못 들었어요 uses -는 바람에: the internet outage disrupted the online class.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find all instances of -더니 and -(으)ㄹ수록 in the text. For each -더니, explain what was observed and what changed. For each -(으)ㄹ수록, identify the two proportional elements.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: -더니 instances: (1) 발음이 너무 어렵더니 — observed: pronunciation was difficult; changed: now accustomed. (2) ㄹ과 ㄴ 소리가 비슷하더니 — observed: the sounds seemed similar; changed: now the difference is clear. (3) 드라마 대사가 너무 빠르더니 — observed: drama dialogue was too fast; changed: now the writer roughly understands the content. -(으)ㄹ수록 instances: (1) 공부할수록 더 많은 것이 보이기 시작했어요 — study ↑ → visibility ↑. (2) 어휘가 늘수록 한국 문화도 더 깊이 느껴지는 것 같아요 — vocabulary ↑ → cultural feeling ↑. (3) 노력할수록 보람이 커지는 게 느껴져요 — effort ↑ → fulfillment ↑. (4) 보면 볼수록 매력 있는 언어 — exposure ↑ → charm ↑.

culturalNote.title: 보면 볼수록 — The most Korean way to express growing love for something
culturalNote.body: The phrase 보면 볼수록 (the more you look at/experience it) is a cultural formula in Korean for expressing that something deepens with time and exposure. Koreans use it constantly about food (먹을수록 맛있어 — the more you eat it, the better it tastes), people (알수록 좋은 사람이야 — the more you get to know them, the more you like them), and learning itself (한국어는 할수록 재미있어 — Korean gets more fun the more you do it). It reflects a cultural value of depth through perseverance — the appreciation that comes not at first glance, but after sustained engagement. When a Korean friend says 보면 볼수록 좋아 about something, it is one of the highest compliments possible: this thing rewards continued attention.

inlineExercises.prompt: 비가 오___ 집에서 연습했어요. (I noticed it was raining, so I practiced at home.)
inlineExercises.explanation: -길래 fits because the rain is something the speaker noticed, and practicing at home was the reaction. -기 위해서 would make the rain a purpose, which is impossible. -수록 would require a proportional 'the more...' relationship.

inlineExercises.prompt: 발표를 준비하___ 매일 연습해요. (I practice every day to prepare for the presentation.)
inlineExercises.explanation: Preparing for the presentation is the purpose of daily practice, so use -기 위해서. -는 바람에 would mean an unexpected disruption, and -더니 would report an observed sequence.

inlineExercises.prompt: 갑자기 인터넷이 끊기___ 온라인 수업을 못 들었어요. (The internet suddenly cut out, so I missed the online class.)
inlineExercises.explanation: The internet outage unexpectedly disrupted the plan, so -는 바람에 is the right connector. -기 위해서 gives purpose, and -(으)ㄹ수록 gives proportional change.

inlineExercises.prompt: 친구가 매일 운동하___ 날씬해졌어요. (My friend kept exercising and then became slimmer.)
inlineExercises.explanation: This is a CAMERA REPLAY situation: you personally watched your friend exercise over time (camera rolling) and are reporting the observed result (became slimmer). -(으)ㄹ수록 would express a proportional scale (the more they exercise, the slimmer they get) — ongoing, not a reported sequence. -길래 would mean you reacted to something yourself, which doesn't fit here.

inlineExercises.prompt: 한국어는 공부___ 더 재미있어요. (The more you study Korean, the more fun it gets.)
inlineExercises.explanation: The 'the more X, the more Y' proportional scale pattern requires -(으)ㄹ수록. 하다 has a vowel-class stem 하 → 할수록. -더니 would report an observed past change, not a proportional ongoing relationship. -해서 would give a simple cause-and-effect (I studied, so...) with no sense of proportionality.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다음 문장에서 틀린 것을 찾아보세요: '저는 열심히 운동하더니 건강해졌어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Plain -더니 is for observations about OTHERS. When the speaker describes the result of their OWN past action, the past tense form -았/었더니 is required. 운동하더니 with 저는 sounds like you somehow watched yourself from outside — unnatural. 운동했더니 = after I exercised (my own action), I found that I became healthier.

inlineExercises.prompt: Translate: 'The more experience you gain, the more confident you become.'
inlineExercises.hint: The stem 쌓이- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ수록 attaches as ㄹ수록: 쌓일수록. What word means 'confidence develops'?
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ수록 makes the 'the more X, the more Y' structure. 경험이 쌓이다 and 자신감이 생기다 are natural pairings for experience increasing and confidence appearing.

inlineExercises.prompt: You saw your colleague looking exhausted every day for weeks, and then they took sick leave. Which sentence is most natural?
options: 동료가 매일 피곤해 보이더니 결국 병가를 냈어요.
inlineExercises.correct: 동료가 매일 피곤해 보이더니 결국 병가를 냈어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: Option B (-더니) is correct: you personally observed your colleague looking tired over multiple days (camera rolling), then report the outcome (sick leave). Option A (-ㄹ수록) would mean 'the more tired they looked, the more sick leave they took' — a proportional scale that doesn't match the scenario. Option C (-길래) would mean the tiredness prompted YOU to take an action yourself, not describing their sick leave.

inlineExercises.prompt: 서울은 살___ 더 좋아지는 것 같아요. (The longer you live in Seoul, the more you come to like it.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 살다 is an ㄹ-stem verb. ㄹ-stems drop their ㄹ and attach -(으)ㄹ수록 as -ㄹ수록: 살다 → 살 + -ㄹ수록 → 살수록. This expresses the proportional scale: time in Seoul ↑ → appreciation ↑. -더니 would report an observed change (you watched and noted a result), not a proportional relationship. -아서 is a simple cause connector.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses -(으)ㄹ수록 with the correct attachment?
inlineExercises.explanation: 읽다 ends in a consonant cluster (ㄱ final). Consonant-ending stems take -을수록: 읽 + 을수록 = 읽을수록. Option A (읽수록) skips the vowel buffer -을 needed after a consonant — this is wrong. Option C (읽어수록) confuses the polite ending 어요 with the -수록 attachment — 수록 never uses the -아/어 vowel; it attaches via -을/ㄹ.

inlineExercises.prompt: 발표___ 준비하기 위해서 매일 연습해요. (I practice every day to prepare a presentation.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 준비하다 takes the thing being prepared as an object, so 발표를 fits. 가 would make 발표 the subject, not the preparation target.

inlineExercises.prompt: 서울은 살___ 더 좋아져요. (살다 → the more)
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ수록 means “the more.” 살다 has ㄹ already in the stem, so the natural form is 살수록.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'The internet suddenly cut out, so I missed class.'
inlineExercises.correct: 갑자기 인터넷이 끊기는 바람에 수업을 못 들었어요
inlineExercises.explanation: -는 바람에 frames the cause as an unexpected disruption. 못 들었어요 gives the bad result that followed.

bullets: -더니 = CAMERA REPLAY: you watched X happen (about someone else or a situation), then Y followed — use -았/었더니 for your OWN past actions
-길래 = NOTICED AND REACTED: a clue caught your attention, so you did something
-는 바람에 = DISRUPTED CAUSE: an unexpected event caused an unwanted result
-(으)ㄹ수록 = SLIDING SCALE: as one thing increases, another increases proportionally — the -면 V-ㄹ수록 form is the most natural spoken version
-기 위해서 = PURPOSE ARROW: a planned action points toward a goal

writingTask.prompt: Write a short story in one connected paragraph about how a late-night snack habit led you to a decision, joining your ideas smoothly.
writingTask.hint: Connect clauses with -더니, -길래, -는 바람에, -(으)ㄹ수록, and -기 위해서.
writingTask.model: 친구가 야식을 자주 먹더니 살이 많이 쪘어요. 저도 배가 고프길래 같이 먹었어요. 그런데 늦게 자는 바람에 다음 날 너무 피곤했어요. 야식은 먹을수록 끊기 어려워서, 건강을 지키기 위해서 이제 안 먹기로 했어요.
writingTask.modelEn: My friend kept eating late-night snacks and then gained a lot of weight. I was hungry too, so I ate with him. But because I went to bed late, I was so tired the next day. The more you eat midnight snacks the harder they are to quit, so to protect my health I've decided not to eat them anymore.

canDo: Link what I noticed to what followed (-더니)
Give the outside trigger behind my own reaction (-길래)
Blame an unexpected cause for a bad result (-는 바람에)
Express 'the more…, the more…' (-(으)ㄹ수록) and state a purpose (-기 위해서)
